item.title: Cowboys’ CeeDee Lamb is seeking revenge on Cardinals in Week 8 after massive losing streak
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Cowboys’ CeeDee Lamb is seeking revenge on Cardinals in Week 8 after massive losing streak appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It seems like the rumors are flying around George Pickens and the Dallas Cowboys . But what’s next is the matchup against the Cardinals . And CeeDee Lamb is seeking revenge on the Cardinals in Week 8 after a losing streak , according to a post on X by Todd Archer. “CeeDee Lamb was asked about a ‘heightened awareness’ this week for the Cowboys because Arizona beat them last year. ‘I’ve never beat the Cardinals since I’ve been in the league, so that’s kind of fair to say,’ Lamb said.’I wouldn’t say heightened focus, but it’s definitely another take.’ ” What’s up with the Cowboys losing to the lowly Cardinals? Arizona has won four straight (2020, ’22, ’23 and ’25) and three have been at AT&T Stadium. Lamb said the Cardinals have been a different bunch when they play the Cowboys. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “They’ve always had more energy,” Lamb said. “Just coming out in the game, they’re more excited regardless of if it was at 12 o’clock, Sunday night, Monday night. We played them in primetime. They beat us there. So just coming in, treating them as if they are a Super Bowl-contending team, which they may be, you know what I’m saying? So hats off to them in their prep. And we just got to go match them, if not overpower them.” Uh, the Cardinals may be a Super Bowl-contending team? Seriously? Why do the Cowboys need to invent fake narratives to get themselves fired up for an NFL game? Weird stuff. One good thing for the Cowboys is they are coming off an impressive offensive performance — even if it was against a team that looked mailed in over the last 15-20 minutes. Lamb said the Cowboys rediscovered their identity , according to dallascowboys.com. “No, that’s exactly who we are. We’re better balanced,” he said. “We could beat you in a run game. We could beat you in the pass [game].” Individually, Lamb says defenses cannot guard him. “I think my ability to line up anywhere in the offense and run any route on the route tree,” Lamb said. “I feel like I could (beat) anybody in front of me, and I’m standing on that.” Related: Cowboys rumors: Is George Pickens trade a serious possibility after Brian Schottenheimer callout? Related: Giving up 2 catches this season has Cowboys’ Joey Porter Jr. ‘pissed’

item.title: Columbus Blue Jackets come up short against Carolina Hurricanes
item.description: They finished strong in a road matchup against the reigning Stanley Cup champions, but the Blue Jackets couldn't overcome a three-goal deficit in a 3-2 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes on Oct. 29 in Raleigh, North Carolina. More: Cam Talbot continues to shine in Columbus Blue Jackets' OT win Denton Mateychuk and Kent Johnson scored goals 2:54 apart to pull the Blue Jackets (5-6-0) within 3-2 in the third period, but Mark Jankowski's goal for Carolina 16 seconds into the period was the difference. Hurricanes goalie Pyotr Kochetkov (24 saves) didn't allow another goal despite the Jackets pushing late with their net empty for a 6-on-5 advantage. Mateychuk cut it to 3-1 at 6:56 of the third to extend his goal streak to three straight games and Johnson followed by capping a power play at 9:50 for his seventh goal of the season. There just wasn't a tying goal in the cards for the Blue Jackets, who got 24 saves from goalie Jet Greaves in his first game since taking the loss Oct. 20 against the Toronto Maple Leafs . Jordan Martinook and Logan Stankoven scored the first two goals for the Hurricanes (11-2-2), who've won four of their past five games and sit comfortably atop the Metropolitan Division with 24 points and a cushion of eight points over the New Jersey Devils in second. The Blue Jackets will wrap up their first multi-game road trip of the season Oct. 31 in Dallas. item.title: Luka Doncic cleared for injury return in Warriors clash
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Luka Doncic cleared for injury return in Warriors clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After being sidelined against the LA Clippers due to a back issue , Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic was off the team’s injury report ahead of their upcoming game on the road against the Golden State Warriors on Friday. Prior to Wednesday’s win against the Clippers, Lakers head coach JJ Redick acknowledged that Doncic’s status was nothing overly concerning, just precautionary as the team heads into a stretch of five games in seven nights. In addition to Luka Doncic, the Lakers might get forward Ziaire Williams back from injury as he was listed as questionable against the Warriors. Williams also was ruled out against the Clippers in similar precaution. The sixth-year wing signed with the Lakers in the offseason via free agency, and has been among the team’s most consistent players to this point as a starting forward. With Doncic back in the lineup, however, the on-court antics are certainly going to draw headlines as much, if not more, than the actual basketball. During the Lakers’ season opening win against the Warriors back on Oct. 21, Doncic was engaged in a trash-talking battle with Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg . Doncic got the better of that matchup, which included burying a half-court bomb to beat the halftime buzzer. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) After the game, both players acknowledged the chatter throughout the game, but Lendeborg took it a step further, proclaiming he had lost respect for Doncic due to his perceived complaining to the officials. Lendeborg was hit with a technical foul during the game, with teammate Draymond Green coming to his defense about. For the Lakers, the return of their star player is a much welcome development. The Slovenian native has gotten off to a blistering start to the season, and is among the early MVP candidates. He dropped a season-high 52 points last Sunday to help the Lakers grab a come-from-behind win against the Utah Jazz, and he followed that up with a 41-point effort despite a loss to the Portland Trail Blazers. Across the first four games of the season, Doncic is averaging a league-leading 36.0 points, 6.8 rebounds, 8.3 assists and 1.3 steals with splits of 48.4 percent shooting from the field, 39.6 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 87.5 percent shooting from the free-throw line. He is also currently leading the league in 3-point shots made and attempted, and free-throws attempted. item.description: UFC BJJ 13 happens on THURSDAY (October 29, 2026) inside the UFC’s Meta Apex venue in Las Vegas, Nevada. The event will be topped by two title bouts, and will also feature CJI and ADCC champions returning to the promotion. Mikey Musumeci ’s belt will soon have a new owner after the first and only UFC BJJ bantamweight champion has decided to relinquish his title to “prioritize MMA training” and fun jiu-jitsu matches as he ends his “serious” grappling career . Competing for the now vacant belt is Musumeci’s training partner and two-time world champion Jalen Fonacier , with the Filipino-American grappler taking on Kleber Barboza . That bout will be on the co-main event, with the actual headliner being another vacant title bout featuring Jay Rodriguez and William Tackett , who will receive his second shot at a UFC BJJ belt. Jay’s more popular brother and CJI champ Nick Rodriguez will also be on the stacked card against recent IBJJF Pan-Am champ Nata Tenca . The stacked card also features reigning and former ADCC champions’ returns, with Jasmine Rocha and Ffion Davies being on separate bouts. CJI vet and champion wrestler Pat Downey also makes his debut on the deep UFC BJJ 13 line up. The no gi Brazilian jiu-jitsu (BJJ) event will stream LIVE on UFC Fight Pass, starting at 8 p.m. ET . item.description: LEXINGTON — The Lexington Lady Lex found out the hard way the importance of starting soccer games off the right way. In their 2-1 Division III district championship loss to Elida on Thursday, Oct. 29, Lady Lex experienced a slow start and took a little too long to get things going. The loss ended their season with a 13-4-3 record. “I felt like we played with a lot of nerves,” Lexington coach Buck Morton said. “We never got the ball down to our feet. We knew that this would be a different level of game just from watching them on film and seeing that they moved more athletically and played with physicality. We knew it would be a tough game, but we had to play through not great touches.” KEEP UP WITH THE POSTSEASON: 2026 fall sports postseason tracker | Clear Fork wins girls soccer program's 10th district title Elida scored the opening goal off of a corner kick with 27:06 remaining in the first half and the score stood 1-0 into halftime. Lexington sophomore Jersie Palmer evened things up with 30:21 remaining when she rebounded a Morgan Harrod shot that drilled the post and bounced perfectly back to Palmer who finished the goal. Lady Lex saw two more shots go off the cross bar and one more off the post as they were literally inches away from taking the lead multiple times. “We gave up a really soft goal on the cross. Lexie Good drilled the penalty kick to the upper 90 and gave Elida the lead and eventually the win. “I just didn’t agree with the call,” Morton said. “The ball was clearly away and nothing like that was called all night long and it was awarded with a PK. item.title: Panthers start TNF on fire by forcing kickoff fumble vs. Packers
item.description: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Panthers start TNF on fire by forcing kickoff fumble vs. Packers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Carolina Panthers faced a defensive dilemma before facing the Green Bay Packers . But set the tone on special teams during their road trip to Lambeau Field. Jackson Kuwatch and Nick Hampton became responsible for igniting the Panthers’ side early. Coleman Owen retrieved the opening kickoff from his own eight-yard line. Owen fielded it back to the 27-yard line, but lost control of the football on this Kuwatch hit. WHAT A START TO TNF 🍿 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Panthers force the Packers fumble on the opening kickoff and RECOVER! pic.twitter.com/kWBsS08fXK — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 30, 2026 Hampton became the defender on the spot to pounce on the loose football. It marks the first time this season that the Panthers recovered the opening kickoff. Plus also becomes the first fumble recovery by the Panthers’ special teams unit this season. Carolina and quarterback Bryce Young were handed a very short field to work with. Coach Dave Canales kept things simple in that sequence, trusting the ground attack with three running plays. Young, though, took a costly sack by Devonte Wyatt on third down. The Panthers settled for the field goal in completing the six-play, eight-yard drive following the fumble recovery to go up 3-0. Carolina walked into the historic NFL venue with a 3-3 overall record. But are fresh off receiving a rough 43-13 defeat at the hands of the fierce NFC South rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers from Sunday. The loss became the most one-sided defeat this season for Canales and the Panthers. Carolina struggled to move the ball during its second possession, going three-and-out and sending the punt team out. Then Packers quarterback Jordan Love found tight end Tucker Kraft for a 12-yard red zone touchdown to place GB up 6-3. Snow recalled the raucous atmosphere at Anaheim Stadium for Game 7 of the 2002 World Series. Those were the days of the Rally Monkey mascot and fans banging Thunderstix, but Snow savored the setting even if the Giants lost. "It was probably more electric than any game I've ever played in my whole life," he said in 2016. "You could sense it everywhere, from the clubhouse to the field during batting practice. Before that, Golden State bounced back from an 11-point halftime deficit to beat Chicago in Game 7 of the 1975 West finals (yes, the Bulls were in the West back then). The Warriors subsequently swept Washington to win the NBA title. More than 40 years later, Barry remembered the tension - and agonizing first half - of that Game 7 against the Bulls. "I remember stinking up the gym and sitting on the freaking bench, praying for my teammates to do well," he said in 2016. "They did, and held the Bulls scoreless for seven minutes. Thankfully, I came back in and made some shots. … "I also remember losing to Phoenix the next year, which was heartbreaking. We should have won that Game 7 and didn't. So I have great memories

item.title: Red Wings interim GM admits Dylan Larkin trade is ‘difficult’ for this reason
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bob Frid-Imagn Images Red Wings interim GM admits Dylan Larkin trade is ‘difficult’ for this reason appeared first on ClutchPoints . The Detroit Red Wings have had a difficult season to this point and they find themselves tied for the bottom spot in the Atlantic Division of the Eastern Conference. In addition to trying to find a winning formula, they have had to deal with the trade demand of Dylan Larkin , their former captain. "I got to give Dylan a lot of credit. He went out and played hard for us. Dylan's been here for 12 years. In terms of sitting out, I can't put a timeline on it. With the teams on his list a trade is difficult." pic.twitter.com/NCgPsiZnhY — BucciOT.Com (@Buccigross) October 29, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) After making his demand public, Larkin played multiple games for the Red Wings before he let them know that he was not reporting to practice. As a result, the Red Wings have suspended Larkin without pay. “Dylan Larkin has informed us that he will no longer play for the Detroit Red Wings,” interim GM Shawn Horcoff said in a statement. “We are disappointed by his decision, particularly given his obligations to the organization and his teammates. We have therefore suspended Dylan without pay.” They are still trying to trade him, but Larkin has a list of just 10 teams that are on his accepted trade list. According to Horcoff, the limited number of teams on Larkin’s trade list makes it more difficult for t he Red Wings to make an acceptable trade . Horcoff has said on multiple occasions that the Red Wings would only make a deal that is beneficial to the team. Horcoff said he appreciated the effort that Larkin demonstrated in the 10 games that he has played this season for Detroit. Larkin had 2 goals and 4 assists in those games. Alex DeBrincat leads the team in scoring with 6 goals and 7 assists in 12 games. Veteran forwards Lucas Raymond and Viktor Arvidsson are right behind DeBrincat with 11 and 10 points, respectively. With the Baltimore Ravens taking on the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, the team’s defense will have a tall task in looking to at least contain superstar quarterback Josh Allen. As it remains to be seen if Lamar Jackson returns from injury for the Ravens against the Bills, the defense will still have to do their part, as defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver speaks about the challenge and even jokes with a reporter about the topic. Talking to the media on Thursday, Weaver was asked about the challenge of stopping Allen, saying that it will “take all of us” to stop him. So far this season in six games, he’s recorded 1,504 passing yards with nine touchdowns and four interceptions, plus 240 yards and eight scores on the ground. “Same as it always is, right? Take takes all 11,” Weaver said, according to Jamison Henley of ESPN. “You got to stop the run, right? First and foremost, try not to give him 50-50 run-pass situations, and we know anytime it is a pass, that can turn into a run too with Josh [Allen]. So, tremendous challenge, tremendous quarterback. We know he’s elite, so it’s going to take all of us.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said “it’s going to take all of us” when it comes to defending Josh Allen . A reporter later pointed out that Baltimore hasn’t allowed a lot of scrambling yards this year, Weaver said: “So, are you’re trying to jinx us now?” pic.twitter.com/P1MOIEK3lx — Jamison Hensley (@jamisonhensley) October 29, 2026 After answering that, one member of the media would point out how Baltimore actually has not allowed a lot of rushing yards when a quarterback scrambles, leading to a humorous response from Weaver. “A reporter later pointed out that Baltimore hasn’t allowed a lot of scrambling yards this year, Weaver said: ‘So, you’re trying to jinx us now?'” At any rate, it remains to be seen how Allen will play against the Ravens, as the team looks to snap a two-game skid. item.title: Michael Kay defends Pat McAfee: ‘People don’t know what this business is like’
item.description: Credit: The Michael Kay Show; Kirby Lee - Imagn Images Pat McAfee opened up this week about his fears as a public figure and live performer, sparking a full news cycle of industry responses. The daily show host and College GameDay star took issue with the University of Utah for egging on its students to tease McAfee in a social media video, alluding to the murder of Charlie Kirk at nearby Utah Valley University in a long rant on his show Monday. Later, a report revealed the FBI contacted McAfee about his safety after Kirk’s death, which McAfee confirmed on Thursday . While McAfee seemed to leap to the conclusion that the Utes’ social media video could endanger him while he hosted GameDay , longtime New York City sports host Michael Kay defended the controversial ESPN star on his radio show. “Did he extrapolate too much? Well, we don’t know what he’s feeling,” Kay said Thursday on his ESPN New York show. “We don’t know the fear that he has about taking the stage every day in front of all those kids.” Kay then directed his attention toward McAfee’s critics . “People are saying he’s thin-skinned and that he reads everything about him. You’re all full of it,” he said. “Pat McAfee is grilled every single time he opens his mouth. Maybe he’s not your cup of tea, but I’ll tell you what. He’s built one heck of a career, and he’s making a truckload of money. And he’s on every major portal that ESPN has. Everything. Monday Night Football , College GameDay , and then he has his show, which he owns. Brilliant businessman, and knows exactly about the zeitgeist of this country. But we’re going to tell him that he shouldn’t be thin-skinned. You people don’t know what this business is like.” ICYMI: @RealMichaelKay defends @PatMcAfeeShow. https://t.co/Yl1Vhu9Wpj — ESPN New York (@ESPNNewYork) October 29, 2026 Of course, successful public figures often get the most criticism. As Kay acknowledged about his own hyper-awareness toward what the audience is saying, it is part of the job. But Kay defended McAfee’s engagement with that noise as well. “Don’t tell him that he shouldn’t care about the critics or the people that say nasty things about him,” Kay said. “You get in this position. You see what it feels like. You see if it’s fun. You see if it doesn’t make you second-guess some of the stuff you do. Even though most of the people that are saying it, they would have no idea how to do your job, and couldn’t do it one-hundredth as well as you do.” Some of what the Utes’ video teased McAfee about, and what fans dislike about him, relates to his persona as a sports host. But much of the disdain for McAfee also comes from the guests he books, his commentary on political and social issues, and his frequent embrace of the Trump administration. McAfee noted this in a post on X following his on-air monologue. McAfee complains that outlets take him out of context and don’t cover him fairly on these matters. He often pushes back against media narratives when he feels wronged.

item.title: Colts RB Jonathan Taylor is the last longstanding veteran pillar remaining, for now
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 18: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts warms up prior to the game against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Thursday, Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor, who’s arguably the franchise’s last longstanding veteran cornerstone still remaining after the recent trades of both Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, indicated that he has not requested a trade from the only organization he’s ever known. However, he did acknowledge his current uncertain future, which still appears to be very fluid in Indianapolis: #Colts RB Jonathan Taylor confirmed that he has *NOT* requested a trade, but he acknowledged that he doesn’t have full control of his future. — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) October 29, 2026 As a major subject of ongoing trade rumors, Taylor seems proud and comfortable to continue to wear the Horseshoe, and earlier reports indicated that Indianapolis team owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon potentially considers Taylor a major part of the Colts recently jumpstarted rebuilding efforts . That being said, Taylor is 27-years-old with 1,691 career carries in the NFL and 926 more collegiately at Wisconsin, at a running back position where players typically don’t age gracefully past the age of 30-years-old. Either the Colts or an acquiring team are realistically looking at 2-3 prime years left regarding Taylor, and for Indianapolis, that’s likely about the minimum amount of time that it would take to complete a successful rebuild these days—assuming conditions go well with a new quarterback, head coach, and general manager all likely. However, keeping a future Colts Ring of Honor player and potential Hall of Famer in the building around young players could be a beneficial thing as far as teaching them an elite work ethic, preparation, approach, etc. It seems to me that the Colts could be persuaded to trade Taylor soon, but it would have to take a significant haul in draft capital from a suitor, presumably the ask right now appears to be at least a first round pick, maybe more. Whether that asking price will go down, like say a second round pick, as we get closer to this year’s trade deadline on Tuesday, November 10th, remains to be seen. However, for now, Taylor is still remaining in Indianapolis.

Reaves finished the game with 8 giveaways.” Jones is averaging 12.5 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.8 assists, and 1.8 steals on 57.6% shooting in four games so far this season, the best averages of his 11-year career so far. However, Jones might be a slight upgrade from all of them. “Even so, if February comes around, and Rob Pelinka wants to make an all-in push before the deadline, one would imagine Jones near the top of the targets list,” Rovenchuk added about the team’s forward depth. “There were murmurings in the offseason about the Clippers’ willingness to operate in good faith so Jones can get to his next team, should that be something he wants before his contract expires at season’s end. Previously, it was Maxwell Odgen, who named the 29-year-old a ‘dream outcome’ and ‘ultimate’ wing for the Lakers to go after in a deal. “The dream outcome here would be for Derrick Jones Jr. to end up with the Lakers. Jones is an elite wing defender who excels at the point of attack, as well as a capable three-point shooter who played alongside Doncic when the Mavericks made their run to the NBA Finals,” he wrote. “Compounded by his experience alongside Doncic, Jones is the ultimate trade target. It could prove costly to bring him on, but with an expiring contract and an ideal skill set for Los Angeles’ system, it’s at least worth exploring.” More recently, answering questions on a Reddit AMA , Lakers reporter Dan Woike of The Athletic brought Jones’ name back up as a realistic Lakers trade target, as the Clippers could make him available in a deal. “I’ve heard the Clippers really value Derrick Jones Jr. as a player and behind the scenes, but if he were available, the Lakers would probably call and hope it turned out better than their last deal with LAC,” Woike said. On fit alone, and given his experience playing with Doncic, Jones is exactly the type of player the Lakers wanted this summer but failed to land. He wouldn’t need the ball in his hands much, but he’s above average on both ends, while offering spacing and some rim-running ability to get easy looks from Doncic, Reaves, and Collin Sexton in the two-man game. Playing Jones alongside Walker Kessler would boost the Lakers’ defense, which they could use, and though it’s uncertain what the Clippers would want back in a trade, if using Jarred Vanderbilt ‘s contract, along with Jaden Hardy or a second-round pick, can get a deal done, that might be worth it for general manager Rob Pelinka to pick up the phone. The Lakers already filled the backup center hole with a low-risk move, but if the team is ready to take a bigger gamble, Jones might be the best trade target available in the final year of his current contract. item.description: KANSAS CITY, Mo. — The school of champions? That certainly has a nice ring to it for one Kansas City metro school. Park Hill High School saw two of their former athletes win championships in a major professional sport in the same calendar year. It started with Landry Shamet, who made huge contributions off the bench en route to the New York Knicks winning the 2026 NBA Finals. Shamet shot 91.7% from three, the highest ever three-point percentage for a single playoff series with at least 10 attempts. The two have a well-documented friendship that started at a sport neither plays: A Park Hill High School football game. The two have shown vast amounts of support each other. Ashby was seen wearing Shamet's jersey back in June, while the Knicks were in the finals, and Shamet rocked Ashby's jersey before Game 1 of the World Series last week. Mizzou RB Ahmad Hardy to play in first game since being shot "We grew up together going to high school and basically became best friends. He's just an amazing human being," Ashby said back in June. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
